name: Saffire-I to III
description: Large fires on an uncrewed cargo spacecraft: fabric and plastic samples burn in a flow duct to show how flames spread and grow.
criteria_basis: Scale: spacecraft-sized duct. Smoke 0.5: telemetry has smoke channels, but I-III detector results were not in sources read. Atmosphere 0.5: flow speed varied (20 and 25 cm/s; III planned near 30). Listed in NASA's PSI call.
psi_id_status: PSI-98 page exists (contents not readable here); ID per author's DOI link

name: Saffire-IV to VI
topic: large-scale fire spread, heat release, gas hazards
description: Larger spacecraft fires measuring heat release, temperature, smoke and toxic gases, at several pressures and oxygen levels.
criteria_basis: Free volume 16.7 to 19.0 m3; pressure 54 to 100 kPa and oxygen 22 to 31 percent across tests; smoke alarm threshold measured. Not in the PSI list read.

name: SAME
description: Measures the size of smoke particles made by heated Teflon, Kapton, cellulose, silicone rubber and a wick-fed liquid, to judge spacecraft smoke detectors.
criteria_basis: Spacecraft materials; detector assessment is the stated aim; airflow, heating temperature and smoke age varied.
psi_id_status: PSI-102 page exists and surfaced for SAME (contents not readable here)

name: SAME-R
description: Reflight in 2010 with Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber and Pyrell, adding electron microscopy of collected smoke particles.
criteria_basis: As SAME.

name: BASS
description: One of the first investigations into putting out fires in microgravity, since ground methods may not work or may worsen a flame.
criteria_basis: Variables not stated in sources read, so atmosphere is 0.

name: BASS-II
program: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
topic: flame spread and extinction of solid fuels
description: Burned acrylic films, sheets, rods and a sphere, plus a cotton-fiberglass fabric, at airflows of 5 to 50 cm/s and varied oxygen to map spread and extinction.
criteria_basis: Oxygen varied by nitrogen dilution and flow 5 to 50 cm/s; quenching boundaries studied; pressure not varied.

name: FLEX
description: Tested how well fire suppressants work on burning fuel droplets and led to the discovery of cool flames.
criteria_basis: Suppressant tests (variables not detailed in sources read).
psi_id_status: reported by a third-party repository; not verified

name: FLEX-2
description: Studied how quickly fuel droplets burn, when soot forms, and how liquid fuel mixtures evaporate before burning.
criteria_basis: No suppression or atmosphere variable stated in sources read.

name: ACME Burning Rate Emulator
description: Burns gaseous fuel to imitate the flammability of solid and liquid materials; 59 burn tests may show if today's flammability tests work in microgravity.
criteria_basis: Emulates solid fuel with gas, so solid materials 0.5.

name: ACME CLD Flame
description: CLD Flame (coflow laminar diffusion flame). NASA's booklet describes ACME as five experiments for the Combustion Integrated Rack (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame) focused on soot processes, flame stability and extinction, materials flammability and electric-field effects. This experiment is not described separately there (overview only). The booklet calls SLICE a precursor to CLD Flame.
criteria_basis: Overview only: not separately described in the sources read.

name: ACME E-Field Flames
description: E-FIELD Flames. NASA's booklet describes ACME as five experiments for the Combustion Integrated Rack (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame) focused on soot processes, flame stability and extinction, materials flammability and electric-field effects. This experiment is not described separately there (overview only).
criteria_basis: Overview only: not separately described in the sources read.

name: ACME s-Flames
description: s-Flame (spherical flame). NASA's booklet describes ACME as five experiments for the Combustion Integrated Rack (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame) focused on soot processes, flame stability and extinction, materials flammability and electric-field effects. This experiment is not described separately there (overview only).
criteria_basis: Overview only: not separately described in the sources read.

name: CFI
description: Cool-flame investigation (name per NASA's PSI list). NASA says cool flames were discovered in FLEX and can continue after the visible flame is gone.
criteria_basis: Name from PSI list; context from NASA page.
psi_id_status: reported by a third-party repository; not verified

name: SPICE
description: Investigated the transition from non-sooting to sooting flames, aiming at simple predictions of soot emissions. Ran in 2009 in the ISS glovebox; its hardware was reported as reused for SLICE and BASS.
criteria_basis: Soot-emission study, not a detector or suppression test.

name: SLICE
program: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
description: Used the SPICE hardware to study lifted and lifting flames in the glovebox, for fuel efficiency and lower pollutant emissions. Operations started and completed in 2012. No findings are reported in the booklet.
criteria_basis: Flame-structure study, not a detector or suppression test.

name: DAFT / DAFT-2
program: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
description: NASA's booklet describes it as the Dust Aerosol measurement Feasibility Test, which examined background aerosol particulate levels on the ISS. No results are stated there.
criteria_basis: Aerosol measurement is relevant to smoke-detector background; no detector was tested.

name: SoFIE-GEL
description: Burned solid spherical samples; observations agreed with model trends for how fuel temperature affects flammability.
criteria_basis: Not in the PSI list read.

name: Confined Combustion
description: Studied flame spread in confined spaces of different shapes; confinement can raise or lower solid-fuel flammability depending on conditions.
criteria_basis: Not in the PSI list read.

name: FLARE
platform: Ground tests (1 g and parabolic flight); ISS KIBO flight tests planned
topic: method to estimate microgravity flammability limits
description: International project to build a method that links material flammability limits in normal gravity to those in microgravity, using ground tests and theory, with ISS flight tests meant to verify it. Aims at a new screening test for spacecraft materials.
criteria_basis: Method development, not a measurement set: no numbers stated on the page. Not in the PSI list read.

name: FM2
program: Flammability of Materials on the Moon
platform: Lunar surface (planned); ground tests in a drop-tower centrifuge
description: Planned first combustion experiment on another planetary body: four fuel samples burned one at a time in atmospheres planned for lunar habitats, with cameras and temperature, oxygen and CO2 sensors. NASA's page gives no flight schedule or results.
criteria_basis: Planned lunar-gravity test with no data yet, so partial gravity stays 0 and it is not in PSI. The challenge text says PSI has no partial-gravity data yet and expects some from FM2 and LUCI.
